offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

proposed.why: The metrics show signature rejections starting right after the receiver's v2 secret deploy, with successful queuing stopping at the same time. That explains the unacknowledged webhooks.

diagnosis.hypothesis: At 21:14:59 webhook-receiver was redeployed with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, and nothing else changed. The provider (fake-provider, not redeployed) still signs its webhooks with the secret the receiver used before. Since that deploy the receiver rejects every webhook as bad_signature and puts none on provider-events. The provider never gets an acknowledgement, so it keeps re-sending. The backlog of unacknowledged webhooks grows (131 at the last evaluation), and the money check cannot settle up to its cutoff. The rejection rate keeps climbing (2.5/s to 19.3/s) because the retries pile up on top of new events. The receiver logged no WARN or ERROR lines for these rejections, so the failure is visible only in the metric. Still open: I did not confirm which secret version the provider uses, and I did not run the money check to see whether anything already booked is wrong. Before the deploy the receiver queued webhooks normally, so the books should only be behind, not wrong.

evidence.shows: All containers are running and healthy. webhook-receiver alone was started at 21:14:59, after the rest of the stack (21:13:33-40).
webhook-receiver is the newest deploy (21:14:59), and its only behavior setting is WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. fake-provider and the consumers were not redeployed.
The receiver logged no WARN or ERROR lines in the last 5 minutes, so the rejections are silent in the logs.
The bad_signature series appears from 21:15:14 and climbs from 2.5/s to 19.3/s. The queued series falls from ~3.9/s and disappears after 21:15:29. Since the deploy, every webhook is being rejected.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to its previous settings, i.e. the webhook secret version the provider still signs with. The provider's retries should then be accepted and queued, and the consumers will catch up. Afterwards, check that bad_signature drops to zero and queued recovers, then run money_check with wait=true. If the secret rotation is meant to stay, coordinate it with the provider and accept both versions during the switch.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Only webhook-receiver is recreated, so webhook intake pauses briefly. The provider keeps retrying, so nothing is lost. After the rollback, a burst of retried webhooks will be queued, adding consumer lag for a while. The consumers are idempotent and dead-letter bad events, so duplicates should be booked only once. If v2 was a deliberate security rotation, rolling back undoes that rotation until it is coordinated with the provider.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the old settings make things worse, redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. The provider keeps retrying any unacknowledged webhooks in the meantime.
